answer: Each identity must anchor one current meter to a reef plot, locking a 70-credit bond, serial key-bound to the owner. Each epoch, before the filing horizon closes, the owner files one key-signed speed reading. A reef auditor recomputes the speed from the public tide-current table; a reading 3% off, a reused serial, or a missed horizon burns the bond. The k-th filing costs 36+7(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,532,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-meter ring fails: one meter reports one plot, and its serial cannot serve two owners. An honest agent pays 36 once, bond back after a clean audit.
